meta: Dramas like He Is Psychometric: a power that reads the past, cold cases, and young leads carrying real weight.
standfirst: A boy who reads an object's history by touching it, used to reopen a fire nobody wanted investigated. Watch it as a two-act show, because that is what it is: a light procedural romcom until roughly episode thirteen, then an abrupt hand-brake turn into mystery and grief that squeezes half the plot into four episodes. The per-episode curve climbing to 9.6 by the end says the turn works. The twist is guessable a long way out, the corporate villain never develops, and one death in the back half buys the story nothing.

picks.why: The closest match in the catalog, and it is the same trade. A power that shows you something about a crime, a prosecutor who has to act on it without evidence, and young leads doing melodrama and procedure in the same hour. Difference: the visions are of the future rather than the past, and it is pace 4 with a far more intricate legal structure, so it is busier and better plotted.

Cold cases and the guilt of the people who closed them. Same engine of information arriving by impossible means, same institutional complicity, same focus on a fire or a file that ruined a family. Difference: no romance and comfort 2, and it is a genuine mystery with a hard, unsentimental ending rather than a hopeful one.

A detective forced to work a case with the wrong tools. Shared cast, and the same structure of a present-day investigator reaching into a past he cannot legally access. Difference: romance 0 and much bleaker, with a period setting and a bitter joke about policing that this show has no interest in making.

Powers inherited, hidden, and eventually used to protect a child. Same treatment of an ability as a burden passed down rather than a gift, same tenderness toward young people carrying something adult. Difference: it is a large-scale action series with a state antagonist, so the intimate two-hander at the centre of this show is replaced by scale.

Same director, and the same genre-blending appetite. Kim Byung Soo again mixing supernatural rules, crime and romance, with identical meters across pace, romance, weight and comfort. Difference: it is a fantasy epic with a demon-king mythology, and it is much messier, so the tight sixteen-episode discipline here is not on offer.

An ability that stops working when the person is unwell. Same idea that a power is tied to a psychological state and costs something to use, same gentle handling of young people who did not ask for it. Difference: it is domestic comedy-drama with no crime plot, so the investigation that structures this show is absent.

The same trade, weighted the other way. A young person with an inconvenient gift, a police-adjacent investigation, a serial predator plot and a romance played broad, and the two shows get compared constantly for exactly that recipe. Difference: it puts the comedy and the romance first and treats the crime as the frame, where this one abandons the comedy at the halfway mark and never picks it back up.

against.title: Memorist
against.why: The most-made comparison, and it is the same premise executed worse. A police officer who reads minds, a serial killer, and a plot that collapses in its second half. If the tight construction is what you liked here, this is the cautionary version.

against.title: Alice
against.why: Recommended for the young-leads-plus-mystery combination and the sci-fi frame. It is a time-travel melodrama that spends its runtime on a mother-son reveal and gets confused about its own rules. The pleasure here is a clean investigation, not a puzzle box.

against.title: Tale of the Nine Tailed
against.why: Paired for the supernatural-plus-crime blend and the idol-adjacent casting. It is a romance-driven action fantasy with immortals, and the crime element is a device. He Is Psychometric is a procedural first, and losing that flips the show.
